sun.upright:
The King of Swords sits very still on his throne, sword upright, in no hurry at all. An Aries Sun is the opposite. You want to be the one who moved first while everyone else was still talking about it. When the King decides, he decides once and it sticks. Air feeds fire, so the card isn't fighting you. It gives the drive a reason you can say out loud, and cardinal fire with a good reason behind it is very hard to stop.

The strain is in the sitting. Mars rules Aries and likes a decision made in the doorway. The King makes his in the chair, and he'd make the same one on Friday as on Monday, and that consistency bores you a little. Aries has The Emperor as its own Major, and he holds ground by force of will. This King holds it by being fair and being seen to be, which takes longer to earn. It feels like being asked to justify something you already know is right. You'll also notice, if you're honest, that the calls you made hot last year are the ones you've had to walk back.

At work you may be getting looked at for a role where people have to live with your decisions, and what gets you there is being predictable, which is harder for you than being bold. With a partner it's winning the argument on facts and then noticing they've gone quiet in a way that isn't agreement. Before the next call that affects other people, write down the rule you're using. Use the same rule next time, even when it doesn't suit you.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this King on an Aries Sun turns into someone who has decided and won't hear another word. Mars already gives you speed, and the King's certainty gives the speed a legal-sounding voice, so you're quick and you sound right, and people stop arguing because it's tiring. That isn't the same as them agreeing. The quieter version is just as common with Aries. You know exactly what the fair call is and can't bring yourself to make it, because making it means someone's cross with you, and you'd much prefer to be the hero.

Think of the colleague whose idea you dismissed in a meeting, fast and a bit cutting, and who's gone quiet on you since. Or the family argument you ended with a fact. Go back to one decision you made quickly and ask the person on the other end how it landed. Listen to the whole answer before you defend it.

moon.upright:
With an Aries Moon, it helps to know that air feeds fire, because a thought about a feeling can make the feeling bigger. This Moon needs to act the moment something stirs, and cools just as fast once it has. The King of Swords brings a pause and a look at what's actually happened. Cardinal fire ruled by Mars doesn't love a pause. The two elements do get on, though, and the pause doesn't have to be long.

You know the anger that goes up in a second and is gone in ten minutes. What's new is that you can watch it go up. There's a cool voice in the middle of the heat asking whether this is about the email or about being overlooked, and sometimes that voice is a real help. Sometimes it's air on a fire, and you think your way into a much bigger fury than the email deserved, lying awake building the case with all its evidence. Usually your body tells you which is happening. Hot face and fast breathing usually mean it's feeding, and a slower breath means you're actually sorting it out.

With a partner this looks like finally being able to say why you blew up, a day later and calmly, and them being surprised. Exercise may settle things better than a conversation would, a hard run before the talk. At work it's catching yourself halfway through a reply to someone who annoyed you. Write the angry answer in full, wait an hour, and then send the King's version.
moon.reversed:
The reversed King on an Aries Moon usually means your feelings have been put on trial. Something upset you, and instead of letting it burn out the way this Moon normally would, you've been cross-examining it for days. Was that fair of them. Was it fair of you. Air keeps feeding the fire, so the case keeps growing, and the Mars in you wants a verdict and a sentence. Or you've swung the other way and decided feelings are a waste of time, and you'll just be efficient and get on with things.

Sleep gets short and so does your fuse. A partner asks what's wrong and gets told, in precise detail, what's wrong with them. Let the heat out the Aries way. Go and do something physical and hard for twenty minutes, and keep the case out of your head while you do it.

rising.upright:
Aries rising goes in head first, and people usually read you as brave or a bit much. Draw the King of Swords for your mask and strangers get someone who walks straight up and says what they think, and, oddly, they tend to trust it. Air and fire help each other. The speed stays and picks up a reason, so you come across as someone who's already weighed it, even if you weighed it in the car park.

You may notice people deferring to you sooner than they used to, and that's a responsibility Aries rising doesn't always want. Mars, as your chart ruler, likes the charge. The King likes being right in a way that can be checked later. In the moment those feel very similar, and a month on they feel very different, when someone quotes your first-meeting opinion back at you as if it were policy. Being taken seriously on sight is flattering. It also means your offhand remarks carry weight you didn't intend.

In a job interview this is the candidate who gives a straight answer to the awkward question and gets remembered for it. On a new team it's being asked to settle a dispute in your second week. With a new neighbour it's the blunt comment about the fence that sets the tone for years. When someone asks for your quick verdict, ask them one question first, and hear the answer before you give it.
rising.reversed:
Aries rising with the King upside down can arrive as a verdict before the introductions are done. You meet someone and within five minutes you've told them what's wrong with their plan, and you were right, and they'll never ask you anything again. Mars on the doorstep plus a cold edge of air reads as arrogance to people who don't know you. Or the directness you usually lead with goes stiff and formal, and you sound like a policy document.

New colleagues are where this shows first. They decide you're harsh and start going round you to whoever's softer. A first date can feel like an interview, with you asking the questions. For the next few first meetings, hold your opinion until they've asked for it. If they don't ask, keep it.

sun.upright:
Taurus Suns don't trust what they can't hold. You want the thing proven, built, in the bank, and you've watched plenty of clever people talk themselves into trouble. So this King is an odd visitor. He's all principle and argument, and his element and yours are opposed, talk against proof. There's real friction here and it'd be a lie to call it easy. What the card asks for is something Taurus rarely does, which is to put what you value into words and defend it in the open.

You already know what you think. That's never the problem with a fixed earth Sun. The problem is that you'd prefer to show people, and the King is a card about telling. Venus rules Taurus, so your judgement is really a matter of taste and loyalty, and you can feel slightly cheapened by having to argue for it. It's like being asked to explain why you love your own garden. Taurus's Major is The Hierophant, who goes by what's always worked. The King goes by what's true, and sometimes those part company, and you're the one who has to say so.

Picture the meeting where you're the only person who's actually done the job being discussed. You need to say, in plain words, why the new plan won't work, and then say it again when they don't hear it. With money it might be a family decision, a loan or an inheritance, where fairness has to be spelled out. Write down the three things you won't compromise on. Keep it short, and show it to one person.
sun.reversed:
This King turned over on a Taurus Sun is stubbornness with a reason attached. Fixed earth already digs in, and with the card upside down you've got the argument ready as well. You've decided, you've found the principle that proves you right, and you're no longer really listening. It can also go quiet the other way, letting someone else's clever case run over what you know from experience, because the words didn't come fast enough and it didn't feel worth the fight.

The cost usually lands with a new manager, or a new partner, who meets the flat refusal and never finds out there was a good reason under it. With money, look out for the investment someone argued you into. Pick one opinion you've held for years without testing it and ask someone who disagrees why they do. Sleep on it before you reply.

moon.upright:
What settles a Taurus Moon is physical. Food, sleep, a warm room, the same people round the same table. The King of Swords offers a completely different kind of calm, the kind that comes from understanding what's going on, and earth and air sit on opposite sides, so the two don't naturally meet. Your body knows before your head does. This card wants the head to catch up and say it plainly.

You'll recognise the slow build. Something's been wrong for weeks and your body's been reporting it, the appetite, the heaviness, the stiff neck, and you haven't looked straight at it because looking might mean changing something. Venus rules Taurus and wants things pleasant, and a fixed earth Moon can put up with a lot of unpleasant as long as the routine holds. What the King brings is one clear sentence about what's actually happening. Being made to name it can feel cold. Usually it's a relief within a day.

Sometimes the King is a person, a calm friend or a sister, who says out loud what you've been thinking. Let them. With a partner it might be the conversation about money or the house that you've been putting off because the current arrangement is comfortable enough. With your own body it's the habit that's stopped doing you good, the second glass or the late dinner. Decide one thing, and keep the rest of the routine exactly as it is.
moon.reversed:
When the King lands reversed on a Taurus Moon, the head and the body stop talking to each other. You've decided how you feel about something on principle, your body disagrees, and you're overriding it. Or you're so settled into what feels safe that you've shut out every reasonable argument for change, and anyone who makes one gets the silent treatment. Fixed earth holds a grudge well, and a cold one it holds even longer.

Eating and sleep usually show it first. Then whoever's been trying to reason with you finds you polite and immovable, and a partner can spend a whole weekend making sense and get nowhere. Ask yourself what you're afraid you'd lose if they turned out to be right. Say the answer to them, even if it comes out clumsy.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising meets people slowly. You're pleasant, unhurried, not easily rattled, and strangers take a while to work out how much you're taking in. With this King drawn for your mask, they're finding out quicker. The card puts a clear, level voice on top of your calm, and people read you as someone who knows what they're talking about and won't be hurried. Earth and air are opposed elements, so there's a gap between the soft entrance and the sharp opinion, and the gap is what they notice.

It can unsettle the other person. They expect easy-going and they get a very plain verdict in the same unhurried voice. You may not realise how that lands, because to you you're only saying what's obvious. Venus rules your Ascendant, so the manner stays kind, but fixed earth doesn't soften the content once it's decided. People trust you quickly, and a few of them are slightly afraid of you, and those are sometimes the same people.

In a negotiation, a salary or a rental or a used car, this is exactly the right card. You'll say the number, you'll wait, and you won't fill the silence. Senior people at a new job may ask you for the honest view, because you look like you'll give it. A new friend might hear the same honesty as judgement. When you give a plain opinion to someone you've only just met, add one sentence about why you think it.
rising.reversed:
First meetings can go flat for Taurus rising with this card reversed. The calm reads as cold, and the few words you do say sound like a ruling. Fixed earth looks immovable at the best of times, and with the King upside down you seem like someone who's already made up their mind about the person in front of you. Maybe you have. Or you're sitting on a sharp opinion so hard that you seem blank, and people fill in the blank themselves, rarely in your favour.

A new colleague ends up asking someone else what you meant. A date leaves the first drink sure you weren't interested. Let one warm thing out early, a compliment you mean or a question about them, and give them something to go on.

sun.upright:
Gemini sits inside this King's own territory, so with a Gemini Sun the card is speaking your language, air to air. Mercury rules Gemini, and the King of Swords is what a Mercury mind looks like after twenty years of practice. Same speed and wit, plus one thing a Gemini Sun doesn't always bother with, a position held for longer than a conversation. You're very good at seeing every side. The card wants to know which side you're on.

The same element amplifies, for better and for too much. The better is obvious. Your arguments are sharp, you can see what's wrong with a plan in about ten seconds, and people are listening. The too much is the habit of arguing the other side for fun, which in a King looks like having no side at all. Mutable air likes to keep options open, and Gemini's Major, The Lovers, is all about the choice you've been avoiding. Committing to one view can feel like closing a window you might want later. You'll feel it most when someone asks straight out what you think and you hear yourself offer three possibilities.

At work this is the moment to be the person who decides, not just the one who spots the problem, and it'll be noticed. With a sibling or an old friend it might be settling a long-running argument by saying who was right, including when it wasn't you. Next time you're asked for your view, give one answer, and stay with it until something new turns up.
sun.reversed:
With a Gemini Sun, the reversed King is cleverness with nobody to answer to. The mind's as quick as ever, quicker if anything, since doubled air runs hot, but it's being spent on scoring points. You can take any position and make it sound reasonable, and you've started doing it to get out of things. Or the Gemini side takes over completely and you won't hold any view at all, so nobody can pin a bad call on you, and nobody quite trusts you with a real one.

The sharp comment in the group chat got a laugh and cost you an ally, and you know which one. Friends may be tired of losing arguments to you. When you notice you're arguing for sport, stop and say what you'd actually do in their position. Then leave it there.

moon.upright:
Talking it through is how a Gemini Moon calms down, preferably out loud, with someone quick enough to keep up. A King of Swords drawn for your tides isn't strange at all. Gemini is one of his three signs, the elements match, and the card speaks straight into how you already process a feeling. What he adds is a judge. You've been talking a mood through from every direction, and he says you're ready to reach a finding.

Matching elements double the habit, though. Mercury rules Gemini, and a Mercury Moon can talk a feeling into the ground. You describe what happened to three friends, each time a bit differently, and the feeling changes shape with every telling until you're not sure what it was. The King wants one honest version. Which part actually hurt, and whose fault it actually was, if it was anyone's. Deciding is uncomfortable for you, because it means you can't keep the other versions handy. It also means you can finally stop turning it over at two in the morning.

There's often one friend whose read you trust, whose plain opinion settles you in a way the group chat never does. Go to them. Sleep changes when the racing head has said the thing that's true. With a parent it can be the calm conversation you didn't think you had in you. Write the feeling down as a single sentence, and if it takes more than one, keep cutting.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed on a Gemini Moon usually means the mind has been left in charge of the feelings and made a mess of it. Doubled air goes brittle. You've analysed a hurt so thoroughly that you've argued yourself out of having it, or into a bleak, clever conclusion about people that you half believe. Mutable air can change its mind about a feeling five times a day, and the reversed King makes each version sound final.

Your phone shows it first, the long messages sent late and the scrolling back through old conversations for evidence. Friends get a sharper tongue than they've earned, and sleep gets thin. Put the phone in another room for an evening. See someone in person and talk about anything else.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising usually gets read as bright, chatty and a bit younger than you are. This King adds weight to the brightness. He's air, you're air, and Gemini is inside his own zone, so it isn't a costume. People hear the quickness they expected and find there's a firm view underneath, and they're starting to come to you for answers where they used to come for company.

That shift can be awkward. A mutable Ascendant likes to keep things light and moving, and the King sits still and says one thing clearly. Mercury rules Gemini, so your chart ruler is the planet of words, and words are doing a lot of work for you at the door. The risk with doubled air is coming across as all head. Strangers get the sharp summary of their situation in the first ten minutes, and some of them love it and some feel dissected, and you may not notice which is which.

At a job interview this is the card for being taken seriously, the answer that's quick and also exact. Friends of friends will bring you their complicated stories. On a date you risk being brilliant company and slightly intimidating. When someone new tells you their problem, ask what they want before you say what you think.
rising.reversed:
Gemini rising with the King upside down tends to come across as too clever by half. The wit that usually gets you liked comes out with an edge, and new people feel they're being sized up or quietly mocked. Air on air, turned over, is quick and a little cold. Sometimes you lose your nerve instead, hedge everything, and seem to have no opinion at all, which is off-putting in its own way.

Picture the joke about the process at a new job, heard by the person who designed the process. Or the dinner party debate you won and weren't asked back after. For a while, let the first thing you say to a stranger be kind and a bit boring. The sharp stuff can wait until they know you.

sun.upright:
The King of Swords looks after people too, in his own way. He does it by being fair to them, which sometimes means telling them no. A Cancer Sun does it by being the one they come home to, the one who remembers and holds everything together. Air and water have no quarrel and no natural pull, so the card and your sign need a proper introduction. That introduction is the work. You're being asked to protect your people with your head as well as your heart.

It's hard for a Cancer Sun, and I'd be lying if I said otherwise. The Moon rules Cancer, and a Moon-ruled Sun feels someone's disappointment before it's happened. The King doesn't flinch at disappointment. He makes the fair call and lets people be upset about it, and to you that can feel close to cruelty, even when it's obviously right. The Chariot is Cancer's Major, though, a card about going forward in armour, and you're tougher than your reputation. Cancer is cardinal, a sign that starts things, and you can start this.

In the family it might be the decision about an ageing parent that everyone's waiting for someone else to make. With your own kids, or anyone you're responsible for, it's the rule you set and then keep. At work it's standing up for a colleague in a meeting, with facts. Decide what's fair first, before you think about how anyone will feel. Then work out how to say it kindly.
sun.reversed:
Reversed on a Cancer Sun, this King tends to show up as a hard shell with a rulebook. You've been hurt, or you're afraid of being hurt, and you've switched to cold logic to stay safe. Everything's reasonable and nothing's warm, and the people who know you are confused, because this isn't how you usually are. Sometimes the King is a person instead, someone with authority over you, a boss or a parent or an ex, whose cool verdicts you're still letting set the terms.

Home is where it shows, in house rules that are really about control and in quietly keeping score with a partner. A work email can be perfectly polite and freezing. Find the soft thing you're guarding and tell one safe person what it is. Everyone else can keep getting the shell for a while.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon feels things at full strength, all of them, and remembers them for years. The King of Swords walks into that like a lawyer into a kitchen. Air and water don't fight. They just haven't met. What the card offers is a fair hearing for your feelings, a clear, level look at what happened, who did what, and what you actually need, without being swept off by how big it is.

You'll probably resist it at first. A Cancer Moon's memory is loyal, it keeps old hurts alongside old love, and looking at them coolly feels a bit like betraying them. The King wants you to be fair to yourself and to the people involved, and that fairness is often what finally lets a feeling settle. Cancer is cardinal water, and cardinal water moves. Once you've understood a thing clearly, you may find you can let it go quicker than you expected.

With family this could be seeing a parent's old behaviour for what it was, neither excusing it nor making it the whole story. At home it's working out what you need from the people you live with and saying it without the sulk. The body often loosens once that happens, especially your stomach and your sleep. Pick the memory that keeps coming back and tell it to someone as plainly as you can, the way a witness would.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Cancer Moon, the King is usually someone's voice in your head. A parent, an old partner, a teacher, whoever taught you that feelings were a nuisance. You hear it the second you start to get upset, telling you you're overreacting, and you shut the feeling down and get on with the day with a lump in your throat. Or it's your own voice, grown harsh from being let down, and you've started ruling on people's motives before they've opened their mouths.

The Moon rules this sign, so the body keeps what the head refuses, in your stomach, your sleep, your appetite. At home you might be very organised and very distant. Next time the cold voice says you're overreacting, ask whose voice it is. Answer honestly, and then let yourself be upset for ten minutes anyway.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising usually comes in carefully, feeling out the room before offering much, and people read you as kind and a bit guarded. With this King on the Ascendant, they're getting a firmer version. The shell's still there, but it reads as composure, and strangers take your quiet for authority. Air and water need introducing, and for once your watchfulness and the King's clear head are working together.

The Moon rules a Cancer Ascendant, so the way you come across has always shifted with your mood. The King steadies it. You may find you're walking into rooms and being asked to take charge, or to settle something, because you look like the calmest person there. That's partly true. Underneath you're still reading every face and feeling every awkward pause, and holding that steady front while your moods come and go can leave you wiped out by evening.

Give it three weeks in a new job and everyone's bringing you their worries, and you're quite good at sorting them. With a new group of friends it's being the sensible one, which can mean missing out on the sillier plans. At a family event it might be the in-law who's suddenly deferring to you. Let one new person see you unsure about something small, like which way the station is or what to order.
rising.reversed:
The reversed King on Cancer rising comes across as defensive. You're polite and precise and there's a wall a foot in front of you that new people bump into straight away. With the Moon ruling your Ascendant you shift with your mood, and when the mood is wary the King's cool edge makes you look judgemental, even when you're only nervous. Or you overcorrect and go soft and apologetic, and people who needed a straight answer don't get one.

The new manager thinks you disapprove of them. Someone who tried twice to be friends has decided you don't like them. Tell people you're a bit slow to warm up. Say it lightly, early in the first conversation, and most people are happy to wait.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns want to lead and be loved for it, and usually manage both. The King of Swords leads too, but he's never been bothered about being loved. He wants to be right and fair, and to have his word mean something. The King's air feeds your fire, so the card gives your natural authority something solid to stand on. It's asking you to lead on principle for a while, even when principle is less popular.

That's where it pinches. The Sun rules Leo, and a Sun-ruled Sun wants warmth coming back. When you make a fair call that disappoints someone you like, you feel it in your chest for a week. Fixed fire is loyal, sometimes to a fault, and the King doesn't do favourites. Strength, Leo's own Major, shows a woman calmly holding a lion's jaws, a gentler kind of power. The King's kind is cooler and it doesn't wait for applause. You'll catch yourself softening a decision so it'll be liked, and you'll know you did it.

At work this is being trusted with authority over people who are also your friends, and having to treat them the same as everyone else. With your children, or anyone younger who looks up to you, it's keeping a rule even when breaking it would make you the favourite. With a creative project it's the honest edit. Make the next decision that matters on the facts alone. Tell the person it affects yourself, warmly, and don't take it back.
sun.reversed:
This King reversed on a Leo Sun is pride that's picked up a gavel. You're certain, you're a bit grand about it, and you've started treating disagreement as disloyalty. Fixed fire digs in, and the reversed King gives it the words to sound like justice when it's really hurt feelings. Or you've stopped making hard calls at all, because you can't stand the thought of anyone thinking badly of you.

Someone on your team has been frozen out since they questioned you in front of others, and they know it. At home there may be a row you won where nobody's speaking to you. Think of the last person who told you something you didn't want to hear. Ring them, thank them, and ask what else they noticed.

moon.upright:
What a Leo Moon needs is to feel appreciated, noticed, loved out loud. When that's missing the feeling is big and hot and usually a bit dramatic, and you know that about yourself. The King of Swords brings cool air to it. Air and fire get on, so the card doesn't put the fire out. It gives you enough room to think while you're still warm.

What he gives a Leo Moon is the ability to tell hurt pride from real hurt. In the moment they feel identical. Someone forgot your birthday, a friend didn't ask about your news, your partner didn't notice the effort, and it's all one big hot feeling. The card asks you to sort it, which of those actually matters and which is your pride wanting a fuss made. Fixed fire keeps a feeling going a long time, and with the Sun ruling Leo, it goes straight to how you feel about yourself. Sorting it isn't easy. It's fair to you, though, and to them.

With a partner this might mean saying calmly, the next day, the one thing you need from them, and dropping the rest of the list. With friends it's noticing who actually shows up, and quietly making more room for them. When the body's warm and the head's busy at night, an evening walk helps the heat go. If you feel slighted, give yourself one night before you say anything. In the morning, say the part that's still true.
moon.reversed:
The reversed King on a Leo Moon usually means a feeling has been turned into a judgement. You were hurt, pride took over, and now you've got a whole case against someone, with principles attached, and you're being very dignified and very cold about it. The Sun rules Leo, so underneath this is about how you feel about yourself, and ruling someone out is easier than admitting they got to you.

A partner gets the frosty, generous-looking silence, perfectly polite, and can tell they're being punished without knowing what for. A friend gets cut off over a slight they don't know they gave. Fixed fire can keep that silence going for a surprisingly long time. Tell one person what actually hurt, in a sentence, with no case attached. Then let them answer.

rising.upright:
Leo rising already walks in like somebody important. Add the King of Swords to that entrance and the warmth turns into command. Fire takes to air easily, so it's a natural fit, and people meeting you see someone confident who also sounds like they've thought it through. Strangers defer to you, ask your opinion first, and assume you're in charge.

The Sun rules your Ascendant, and a Sun-ruled front wants to be liked as well as respected. The King doesn't much care about liked. So there's a small split between the warm, generous way you'd like to come across and the cooler authority people are responding to. To you it can feel like being taken seriously at last, which is lovely. Some people find you a bit grand, though, and fixed fire doesn't always notice when it's being grand. You'll probably hear about it second-hand.

At interview this reads as leadership material, and it may get you a role one level above what you applied for. At a party you're the person everyone gathers round to settle an argument. In a new relationship it can make you seem a little out of reach, when really you're nervous. The first time you meet anyone who matters to you, say something slightly silly early on, so they see the warm side before they decide about the rest.
rising.reversed:
A Leo Ascendant with this card upside down can come across as lordly. Big presence, firm opinions, and a way of ending conversations that people find a bit much. The fire's still warm, but the reversed King puts a haughty edge on it, and strangers decide you think you're above them. Or you're overcorrecting after being called arrogant once, and you've gone stiff and careful and nobody can see the warmth at all.

A new team can decide you're difficult before you've done anything. Meeting a partner's friends can go badly because you held court. For the first half hour of anything new, ask more than you tell. Fixed fire takes a while to change a habit, so count your questions if you have to.

sun.upright:
Mercury rules Virgo, so a Virgo Sun already has a mind that's always working, checking, improving. This King's mind never switches off either, and on paper you'd think the two would get on. But he's air and you're earth, and those elements pull against each other. Your thinking is practical. It wants the detail right and the thing working. His is about principle and the final call. The friction is between being the one who advises and being the one who decides.

Virgo Suns are brilliant number twos. You'll spot the flaw, draft the fix and hand it to someone else to sign off. What the King is pointing at is you signing off. That's uncomfortable, because deciding means acting before every detail is checked, and mutable earth always wants one more check. Virgo's Major is The Hermit, alone with his lamp working things out, and that's how you like to work. The King does his thinking in public and puts his name to it.

At work it may be the promotion that means making calls rather than doing the work, and you're not sure you want it, and you'd be good at it. With your health it's the decision you keep researching and not making. With a friend it could be telling them plainly what you think of the plan they asked you about. Pick one decision you've been gathering information on for too long. Make it with what you have.
sun.reversed:
Reversed on a Virgo Sun, the King becomes the harshest critic in the room, and the room is usually your own head. Mercury and mutable earth together are thorough, and when the card's upside down that thoroughness turns into judgement of your work, your body, the colleague who can't spell. You're often right. You're also exhausting to be around, including for yourself. The other version is endless preparation that never quite becomes a decision.

The people who feel it first are the ones who work with you, whose drafts come back accurate and deflating, and a partner who's stopped offering help because it's never done properly. Say one thing you like about someone's work before you say anything else about it. Do the same for your own.

moon.upright:
Order settles a Virgo Moon. The list done, the kitchen clean, the problem broken into steps you can manage. Mercury rules Virgo, so your feelings have always gone through your head first. The King is also a head card, but he's air and your Moon is earth, and earth wants proof where air offers argument. You feel through doing things. He feels through judging them. What he's offering is a verdict on a worry that's been running too long.

You'll recognise the circling. Mutable earth can worry about the same practical thing for weeks, the health niggle, the bill, whether you said the wrong thing at work, doing a little about it every day and never settling it. The King doesn't circle. He looks at the evidence, decides how serious it is and moves on. That feels risky to you, because the worry has been keeping you busy and busy feels safe. It's still the kinder thing to do for yourself.

With your body this might be booking the appointment you've been reading about online, then leaving it to the person whose job it is. At home it's deciding which jobs actually matter and letting the rest go without guilt. With a partner it's telling them what's been worrying you, plainly, so they stop guessing from how hard you're cleaning. Write the worry at the top of a page. Underneath, write what you'd tell a friend who had it.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Virgo Moon, the King is self-criticism in a judge's robes. Every feeling gets examined and found wanting. You shouldn't be tired, you shouldn't be upset, you should have handled that better. Mercury in its own earth sign is thorough, and the reversed card makes it merciless. Sometimes it turns outward and a partner or housemate gets your worry as cold, precise criticism of them.

The body usually shows it first, a tight stomach, a clenched jaw, a restless night of mental list-making. Then the people closest to you start to hear it in your tone. For one day, don't correct anything, yourself included. When the critical voice starts up, answer it the way you would if it were talking to your best friend.

rising.upright:
Modest, neat and quietly competent is the usual first read on Virgo rising, the person who notices what's gone wrong and offers to fix it. Draw the King of Swords here and the modesty goes. People meeting you hear an expert. Mercury, which rules a Virgo Ascendant, is your chart ruler, so words and details already sit at the front of how you come across, and this card gives them authority. You're being believed.

The elements are where it rubs. The King's air works against your earth, and in first impressions that shows as a gap between how practical and humble you feel and how sharp you sound. You think you're making a helpful point. The other person hears a ruling. Mutable earth adjusts well, and you'll see it in their face and soften, but maybe a sentence late. There's real authority on offer, if you'll take it. People want someone to tell them what's correct, and you usually know.

In a new job it's the week-one comment on the process that turns out to be right, and gets you pulled into a meeting above your level. With a new doctor, lawyer or tradesperson it's the precise question that makes them take you seriously. New friends will find you know the best way to do everything, which is useful and a bit wearing. Before you correct someone you've just met, ask if they'd like your view. Most will say yes.
rising.reversed:
For Virgo rising, the King reversed comes across as fussy authority. You meet people and within minutes you've pointed out a mistake, and whatever the mistake was, that's all they'll remember of you. Mercury ruling your Ascendant plus the reversed card's cold edge makes precision sound like disapproval. Or nerves take over and you go so quiet and careful that you seem to be judging silently, which people find worse.

Meeting a partner's family, it's the comment about how the gravy's made. At a new job it's the reputation as a stickler, earned in the first week. Let the first mistake you notice in any new situation go by without a word. Make a note of it if that helps, and see whether it still matters by the end of the week.

sun.upright:
Justice is Libra's own Major, and the King of Swords holds his sword the way she holds hers, upright and ready. With a Libra Sun that's no coincidence. Libra is one of the three airy signs he belongs to, and what he stands for is what your sign is always reaching for, a fair judgement, properly reasoned, that everyone can live with. The card says you're ready to be that person and make the call in your own name.

Air meeting air amplifies, and with Libra what gets amplified is the weighing. You see every side, and you're genuinely good at it. The trouble is weighing for so long that the decision gets made by default, or by whoever pushes hardest. Venus rules Libra and would like everyone to be pleased, and the King accepts that some people won't be. The moment after a fair call is hard for you. You'll want to go and smooth it over with the person who lost, and sometimes that undoes the call. Cardinal air starts things, so once you've decided, you're good at carrying it through.

At work you might be put in charge of something contentious, a restructure or a dispute, because people trust you to be even-handed. In a relationship it's saying what you want in an argument, where you'd normally explain what they want, and letting it stand. With friends it's the group decision you've been quietly managing that needs someone to just decide. Make a call you've been avoiding, and when someone's unhappy about it, stay kind and don't change it.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with this card reversed is fairness gone rigid, or gone missing. Doubled air can turn the love of balance into cold bookkeeping, who did what, who owes whom, a scrupulous tally that's no fun for anyone. Nobody else sees the ledger, which is how the resentment gets so big. Or Venus wins out and you can't make the call at all, so you keep weighing and asking one more person while the decision gets made by someone less fair.

Picture the meeting you chaired where everyone had their say and nothing was decided. Picture the chores at home, and the favours, all counted. Pick one open question you've been weighing for too long and give yourself a deadline. Write it down, and let someone hold you to it.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon needs things to feel fair, and it needs to feel close to someone. Conflict rattles you more than you let on. The King of Swords is air, like your Moon, and Libra sits in his own zone, so he's speaking your emotional language. He's the version of you that can feel an unfairness clearly and say so calmly, without the smile you usually put over it.

What's amplified is the weighing. A Libra Moon works out what everyone else needs before checking in with itself, and with the King around you may find you're finally doing the sums with yourself included. Venus rules Libra and hates to upset anyone. The King doesn't enjoy it either, but he accepts it. You'll feel a strange mix of guilt and relief when you say what's actually been bothering you, and the relief usually wins by the next morning. The risk of so much air is living in your head until you've talked yourself out of a perfectly reasonable feeling, because you can see the other person's point.

With a partner this looks like the calm, clear conversation about the imbalance you've been quietly putting up with. With a friend it's saying no to a favour and not explaining it at length. Your sleep suffers when things feel unfair, and settling the thing lets you rest. When you feel a flash of resentment, treat it as information. Ask yourself what would make it fair, then ask for that.
moon.reversed:
On a Libra Moon, the King reversed tends to show up as feelings managed by committee. You've consulted everyone about how you should feel, weighed their views, and ended up not knowing. Or the need for peace has hardened into a cool, polished politeness no one can get through, and the people close to you can only tell you're upset by how perfectly civil you've become.

You won't admit to the resentment, because admitting it would spoil the balance. Your shoulders and your sleep are admitting it for you. In a falling-out between friends you've heard everyone's side and quietly ended up on nobody's. Before you ask anyone else, ask yourself what you think is fair. Say it, even if it tips the balance a bit.

rising.upright:
Libra rising already comes across as fair-minded and easy to deal with, the person who smooths the first awkward minutes. This King on your Ascendant lets people feel the steel under the charm. Libra is one of his signs and you share his element, so strangers find you pleasant and slightly formidable. They trust your judgement quickly, and they sense you'd tell them the truth, nicely.

Doubled air amplifies the referee in you. People bring you their disputes, ask you to weigh in, assume you'll be even-handed, and you are. Venus as your chart ruler keeps the delivery graceful. The risk is coming across as a bit detached, above it all, pleasantly judging. It's only good manners and clear thinking as far as you're concerned. For the other person it can feel like being assessed by someone very polite. You'll notice people watching your face for the verdict.

In a negotiation this is an excellent card to draw. You'll look calm, fair and hard to push around, and cardinal air knows how to open a conversation on its own terms. In a new group of friends you'll be the one people turn to when two others fall out. On a first date it can come across as cool. If you like someone, tell them early and plainly, so they're not left guessing.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with the King reversed can come across as cool and faintly superior. The charm's still there, but new people can feel a judgement behind it and aren't sure they've passed. Venus on your Ascendant makes the smile easy, and people notice when it doesn't reach your eyes. Doubled air, turned over, goes from graceful to aloof very quickly. Or you can't commit to any view in a first meeting, so you agree with everyone, and people leave having liked you without trusting you.

Two new colleagues compare notes and find you agreed with both of them. At a party there's a polite distance nobody quite gets past. At the next new meeting, say one opinion you hold that might not go down well. Say it gently, and stick to it.

sun.upright:
There's usually something a Scorpio Sun knows and hasn't said. The King of Swords is the card of saying it. In one way you're well matched, because neither of you is afraid of what's true. In another you're strangers. Water and air are neutral to each other, no clash and no ease, and the King's truth is spoken where yours is felt, and mostly kept.

What this card asks of you is to put your judgement on the record. You already know what's going on, you usually knew before anyone else, and you've been keeping it as leverage or as protection. Mars rules Scorpio in the old system, Pluto in the modern one, and either way there's a lot of power in knowing and not saying. The King gives that power up. He says what he knows and lets people watch him say it. Fixed water finds that exposing, and it is. Death is Scorpio's Major, and there may be something that needs ending, clearly, with the reasons given.

At work this is the moment to say what you've seen, with the evidence, in the meeting with people present. In a relationship it's telling your partner the thing you've decided, instead of testing them to see if they'll guess. With money it could be the arrangement with a friend or a relative that's gone murky and needs putting in writing. Choose one truth you've been holding and say it plainly to the person it concerns.
sun.reversed:
This King upside down on a Scorpio Sun is perception turned into a weapon. You know exactly where someone's weak spot is, and you've started using it, precisely and coldly, in the name of honesty. Fixed water holds on, and with the reversed card the grudge acquires a legal argument. Or the King is someone else, an authority you're locked in a quiet power struggle with, and neither of you is going to blink first.

A feud at work can become more important than the work. The people around you can feel it even if they can't name it. At home there's the argument where you said the true thing that couldn't be unsaid. Before you say the next one, ask yourself whether it'll help or only win. If it's only winning, hold it back.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel everything at full depth and trust almost nobody with it. What you need is loyalty and the truth, and you can smell a lie across a room. He's a strange companion for that, the King of Swords. His air and your water have nothing against each other and nothing much in common. He wants the facts. You have the feeling, and the feeling is usually right, and it's also sometimes a very old fear dressed up as instinct.

That's the useful work in this draw. Fixed water holds on to a suspicion for a long time, turning it over, and Mars ruling Scorpio gives it teeth. The King asks you to test it. What do you actually know, what are you inferring, and what are you remembering from someone who hurt you years ago. It's uncomfortable, because the suspicion has been protecting you. It's also a relief, because you've been carrying it on your own. Some of it will turn out to be accurate, and some of it will go the moment you look at it straight.

With a partner this could be the jealousy you've been quietly nursing, looked at honestly for the first time. With a friend it's the betrayal you've assumed and never asked about. In sex and intimacy, where trust matters most to you, it's saying what you need in plain words. Pick one suspicion and ask one direct question about it. Believe the answer for a week before you decide anything.
moon.reversed:
When the King reverses on a Scorpio Moon, feelings go underground and the mind stands guard over them. You've decided not to feel something, and you're being very controlled about it, and the people close to you can sense a cold front without knowing where it came from. Fixed water freezes hard. Or the King's sharpness goes into suspicion, and you're building a case against someone out of small things, with nobody to check it against.

Sleep is often the first to go, then trust, and a partner may be tiptoeing round you. Mars, Scorpio's ruler, keeps a cold grudge going for years if nobody interrupts it. Late at night the case feels airtight. Tell one person what you've been guarding and why. You don't have to act on anything. Just say it where someone else can hear it.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising already has a stare that makes people check their pockets. Put the King of Swords behind that stare and strangers meet someone who seems to see straight through them and to have an opinion about what they saw. That's a lot of presence. His element and yours need introducing, and here the introduction goes surprisingly smoothly. Your watchfulness plus his clear judgement reads as someone you don't lie to.

Mars rules a Scorpio Ascendant, traditionally, with Pluto as the modern ruler, and either way the front you put up is controlled and quietly intense. The King makes it more formal. People may find you harder to read and easier to respect. You might notice rooms going a bit quiet when you speak, or people explaining themselves to you without being asked. You're only paying attention. They feel assessed, and not everyone enjoys that.

This is excellent for anything where you need to be believed, an audit, a hard negotiation, a performance review you're giving. A new partner may find it intense in the good way and then, a few dates in, a bit forbidding. With new neighbours or in-laws it's the reputation for being someone not to cross. Pick one new person and let them see you laugh at yourself. Something small will do, a wrong turn or a bad pun.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising with this card reversed can come across as hostile without meaning to. The stare's the same, but the reversed King adds a cold, judging edge, and people feel under suspicion from the first handshake. Fixed water doesn't warm up fast, and Mars on your Ascendant makes the front look ready for a fight, even when you're only shy. Or you're guarding yourself so carefully that you say nothing at all, and strangers fill the silence with the worst interpretation.

A new colleague decides you're after their job. A date says later that it felt like an interrogation. When you meet someone new, tell them something small and true about yourself before you ask anything about them. The weekend, the dog, the town you grew up in. It gives them a reason to relax.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns are here to find out what's true and tell everyone. You've never been shy about an opinion. The King of Swords is also a teller of truths, but he checks his facts first, and he doesn't change his mind every time he meets someone interesting. Fire loves air and burns brighter for it, so the card fuels your conviction. It also asks you to back it with something solid.

Jupiter rules Sagittarius, the planet of belief and the big view, and the King is a card about sound judgement, so they get on. The tension is speed. Mutable fire likes to jump to the big conclusion and move on to the next adventure. The King sits with a question, looks at it from both sides, and then rules. His pace can feel like a cage, and your honesty is famous for being quick and a little careless. Temperance is Sagittarius's Major, the angel pouring water carefully between two cups, and that's worth thinking about, because your truth lands better with a bit of care mixed in.

At work this might be the chance to become the expert, the one people quote, provided you do the reading. In study it's the qualification that makes your opinion count for more. A friend may ask you for honest advice, and you give it straight and kindly, and it helps. Choose one belief you hold strongly and find the best argument against it. See if your view survives.
sun.reversed:
Opinion hardened into doctrine is what the reversed King tends to mean for a Sagittarius Sun. You've found the truth, and anyone who disagrees is stupid or dishonest, and you've started saying so. Jupiter expands whatever it touches, certainty included. The other form is bluntness without the judgement, the tactless remark justified as just being honest, forgotten by you and not by them.

Think of the lecture nobody asked for, delivered in a meeting to your manager, or the political argument at a family dinner you're still proud of winning. You've usually moved on before the other person has recovered. Before the next strong opinion, ask the person what they think and why. Hear them out properly, and then decide if yours still needs saying.

moon.upright:
Room is what a Sagittarius Moon needs. Room to move, to think, to believe things will work out, and a feeling that life is going somewhere. The King of Swords brings clarity to that, and since air feeds fire it's welcome clarity, the relief of knowing where you actually stand. For a restless Moon, that often feels like more freedom.

What you'll recognise is the habit of skipping past a hard feeling with a big cheerful idea. It'll be fine, everything happens for a reason, let's go somewhere. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and it's generous with hope, and sometimes that's exactly right. The King asks you to look at the thing first, honestly, before you decide it's fine. That honesty can feel like being tied down. Usually the reverse happens. Once you've admitted what's bothering you, the restlessness drops, because the unadmitted thing was what made you want to leave.

With a partner this could be saying clearly that you need more space, instead of disappearing into plans. With a friend it's the honest conversation about the trip that won't happen. Your body needs to move, and the long walk is often where you finally think it through. Next time you feel the urge to book a flight or quit something, write down what you're trying to get away from first.
moon.reversed:
Feelings turned into a philosophy, that's how this card reversed tends to show on a Sagittarius Moon. Something hurt, and you've built a big, rational view about why it doesn't matter, or why people are all like that. Jupiter enlarges, so the view gets grand and a bit cold. Or you've gone blunt with the people closest to you, telling hard truths about them when the truth that needs telling is about you.

Restlessness gives it away, the late nights, the sudden plan to move cities. A partner might get the lecture at the end of a bad week. Mutable fire would always prefer to be moving, and that's fine, as long as you know what you're moving away from. Before you make any big change, sit with the plain feeling for a while. Name it in five words or fewer.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks in friendly and open, full of stories and ready to laugh. With this King as your mask, people are also hearing someone who knows what they're talking about. The elements help each other, and strangers read you as warm, frank and quietly authoritative. Your enthusiasm has weight behind it.

Jupiter rules a Sagittarius Ascendant, and Jupiter is the teacher, the one with the big view. The King sharpens that into judgement. People may ask your opinion on things well outside your field, and you'll give it, because mutable fire loves being asked. The tension is that your candour is fast and the King's is careful. To you it's all just being honest. A stranger's frank opinion carries weight, though, and a throwaway remark can be quoted back to you months later as though you'd ruled on it.

Travelling, you're the person strangers ask for directions and advice. In a new friendship it's the frank read of their situation on the first night, which they'll either love or never forget. At interview you come over as likeable and credible at once, which is rare. At a wedding or a work dinner you'll end up at the centre of the table, being asked what you think. When someone new asks your opinion, give the honest answer, and tell them how sure you are.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising can come across as preachy when the King is reversed. The friendly, frank manner turns into telling people how things are, and new acquaintances feel lectured before they've told you their name. Jupiter ruling your Ascendant makes it big, and the reversed card makes it sure of itself. Or the bluntness gets sharp, and a joke that's meant to be friendly lands as a put-down.

The client who got their own industry explained to them won't forget it. Neither will the stranger at a party who walked off mid-story. Fire and air together travel fast, so it's done before you notice. In your first few conversations with anyone new, ask two questions for every opinion you give. It'll feel slow at first.

sun.upright:
Authority is familiar ground for a Capricorn Sun, earned the slow way, by delivering. The King of Swords has authority too, but his comes from being right and being fair, and that doesn't always line up with getting results. Earth and air are at odds, idea against matter, and that's the friction in this draw. You tend to judge a decision by whether it works, and he judges it by whether it's just, and most of the time those line up.

Saturn rules Capricorn, and Saturn is rules, time and structure, all of which the King respects. Where you part ways is the moment when doing the right thing costs you, the promotion, the contract, the good opinion of someone above you. A Capricorn Sun is very good at telling itself that's how the world works. The Devil is Capricorn's Major, and it's partly a card about what you'll put up with to get ahead. The King won't put up with it. Standing on a principle when it's expensive feels naive to you, and you hate feeling naive. Cardinal earth is good at starting things, though, and it can start this.

At work this could be speaking up about something quietly wrong in how the place is run, with the facts in hand. With money it's refusing a shortcut everyone else is taking. With an older relative, or anyone whose approval you've been chasing, it might mean telling them you disagree. Write down the one line you won't cross at work. Then notice how close you've been getting to it.
sun.reversed:
For a Capricorn Sun, the reversed King tends to show as authority for its own sake. You're in charge, or you want to be, and you've started using rules to keep people in their place. Saturn likes a hierarchy and the reversed card makes it cold. Or the King is someone above you, a boss or a parent, whose rulings you've been obeying long after they stopped making sense, because questioning them feels like failing.

Cardinal earth can keep that grinding on for years before anyone says anything. You enforce the policy you don't believe in. At home, people are afraid of disappointing you. Ask yourself which of the rules you live by you'd actually choose if nobody was watching, and drop one of the others.

moon.upright:
Coping is where a Capricorn Moon feels safest. Feelings are something you deal with, and you're good at dealing. Saturn rules Capricorn, so there's a sense of duty in how you handle your own moods, as if they should be managed like anything else. This King brings a cool head, which you already have, and a sense of fairness, which you may not always apply to yourself.

His air and your earth don't agree, and here that shows as a gap between what you think you ought to feel and what your body's doing. You've reasoned that you're fine. Your shoulders disagree. The King's gift is an honest verdict, and an honest verdict about you would probably say you've been working too hard for too long and are allowed to be tired. Cardinal earth pushes on, and the pushing on is where the stress sits. Being fair to yourself can feel a lot like letting yourself off, which a Capricorn Moon doesn't do easily.

The body keeps count in the neck, the knees, the teeth ground at night, and the rest you keep scheduling for next month. With a partner it's admitting you're struggling, calmly, instead of being short with them. With a parent it can be looking at the high standards you absorbed and deciding which of them are yours. Judge yourself the way you'd judge a good employee who'd had your year, and give yourself what you'd give them.
moon.reversed:
Control is what the reversed King brings to a Capricorn Moon, control used to keep feeling out. Everything's organised, everything's handled, and you aren't letting in anything that might slow you down. Saturn's discipline plus the reversed card's cold logic can make you very efficient and quite lonely. Or it turns to harshness, mostly towards yourself, a running verdict that you're not doing enough.

Stiffness and poor sleep come first. Then the people who love you start getting the managed version of you and not much else, and a partner may feel handled. Take one evening off with nothing planned, and when the urge to be useful comes, sit through it. Put the laptop in a cupboard. If a feeling turns up while you're sitting there, let it stay a while before you do anything about it.

rising.upright:
Picture a first meeting where you haven't said a word and people have already decided you're in charge. That's Capricorn rising on an ordinary day, composed, a bit reserved, older than your years. This King adds a sharp mind to the serious face, and people meeting you see someone who'd be fair and hard to fool. Saturn rules a Capricorn Ascendant, so you've always been read as responsible. The card gets you read as the one who decides.

Air and earth being opposed shows up as a slight coolness in first impressions. You come across as practical and capable, and then you open your mouth and it's more cutting than people expected from someone so steady. You'll see it in their faces. It feels like plain efficiency to you. To them it can feel like meeting a manager on the first day. Cardinal earth likes to start things with a plan, and people will assume you have one, which is handy.

In a pitch, this is about as strong as a first impression gets. You'll look trustworthy and sharp at once. With new neighbours or in-laws it can come across as stiff, and you'll get a reputation for being formal. On a first date you'll be taken very seriously, maybe more than you wanted. Let people see you're approachable early, with something personal, like the thing you do at weekends that has nothing to do with work.
rising.reversed:
For Capricorn rising, the reversed King can make you seem cold and hard to please. The reserve that usually reads as capable reads as disapproval, and people start trying to impress you, or avoiding you. Saturn on your Ascendant plus the reversed card makes the front very stiff. Or you're too careful to commit to any view in public, and people take the silence as judgement anyway.

A new team performs for you and never tells you what's really going on. You leave a party early and someone decides you're a snob. Let people see you not know something. Ask a question that shows it, in front of someone you've only just met. The awkwardness usually lasts about a minute, and people remember it kindly.

sun.upright:
Aquarius is one of the King's own signs, and with an Aquarius Sun he feels like a close relation. Air to air. He's principled, independent-minded, happy to stand apart from the crowd if the crowd's wrong, and all of that will feel familiar. What the card adds is the chair. He's been given the job of ruling, and people are going to be affected by what he decides.

Fixed air holds a view with real tenacity, and Saturn, the traditional ruler of Aquarius, gives it structure and rules. With the element doubled, that can tip into too much. You can be so sure of the principle that you stop noticing the person in front of you. It feels like integrity, and often it is. People close to you can experience that integrity as coldness, though, and you may be surprised to hear it. The Star is Aquarius's own Major, a card of hope, and the King is the part of an Aquarius Sun that has to turn hope into decisions people can live with.

At work this might be leading a change you believe in with people who don't believe in it yet. In a friendship group it's being the one who says the uncomfortable thing about how someone's being treated. With a partner it's standing by what you think in an argument and also hearing what they felt. When you make a principled stand, name one person it'll cost something. Talk to them first.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the King upside down can be right about the big picture and careless about the people in it. Fixed air in its own element, turned over, becomes intellectual stubbornness, and anyone who disagrees gets filed as not having thought about it properly. Or you've gone so detached that you won't take a position at all, and you watch from the side with a clever remark.

The reform you pushed through at work may be one nobody on the ground wanted. With friends, you can be right in the group chat and still not get asked along. Pick one opinion you hold firmly and ask someone it affects how it looks from where they are. Listen for the bit you hadn't thought of.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon handles feelings from a slight distance, and likes it that way. You need space, friends more than fuss, and to be able to think about what you feel before anyone asks you to show it. The King of Swords comes from inside your own element and your own sign's territory, and he makes that distance very comfortable. You can see clearly from there, which is the gift. You'll probably understand exactly what's going on with you emotionally, and that isn't always the case.

The too-much side will be familiar. Fixed air holds a position, and when the position is that you're fine, it can hold it for a very long time. Saturn, the traditional ruler of Aquarius, adds some stoicism, and Uranus, the modern one, adds the urge to pull away suddenly when things get close. It feels calm to you. A partner or a close friend may feel like they're talking to someone reading from notes. The clarity is real, and they'd take it better with some warmth in your voice.

Friends in a crisis find you clear-headed, and you're brilliant at it. A partner hears you explain your feelings very well and doesn't quite get to see any. Your nerves and sleep settle once you've understood something. Tell someone you trust how you feel, using an actual feeling word, and leave the explanation for later.
moon.reversed:
This card turned over on an Aquarius Moon usually means the feelings have been filed away for later, and later hasn't come. You've analysed what you feel, made your peace with it in theory, and gone cool. Doubled air, upside down, can freeze the whole thing so completely that you honestly believe you don't care. Your body may not agree. Or it comes out as cold judgement of people who feel more openly than you do, which is a bit unfair to them.

You might be drifting away from the group without telling anyone why, or needing space just as a partner needed you close. Friends notice before you do. Spend some time with one person you trust, without any particular reason. Let yourself enjoy being near them.

rising.upright:
Strangers find Aquarius rising friendly and hard to place, a bit different from everyone else in the room. This King on your Ascendant sharpens that into someone who clearly thinks for themselves and isn't easily moved. Aquarius is inside the card's own zone and shares its element, and strangers read you as original, principled and a little out of reach. They'll quote your opinions to other people.

Fixed air on the doorway means your first take on something tends to be your final one, and the King makes it sound official. Saturn rules the Ascendant traditionally, Uranus in the modern scheme, so you get both the steady rule-maker and the rule-breaker in how you come across. People find it hard to tell which one they're getting. You feel entirely consistent, because you're following the principle. Others can see someone very conventional one day and very contrary the next.

At work this reads as independence, the person who'll say the plan won't work in front of the director, and be right. In a new group of friends you'll be respected quickly and known slowly. On a first date the other person may feel observed with interest, which isn't quite the same as liked. Let people see one thing you care about as well as what you think.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising with the King reversed can come across as aloof and contrary. You meet people and immediately disagree with something, on principle, and they leave thinking you're difficult. Doubled air turned over makes detachment look like superiority. And once you've taken that first stance, fixed air finds it very hard to walk back. Or you're so determined not to seem cold that you go vague, and people can't tell what you think about anything.

Saturn and Uranus both have a hand in your Ascendant, and a first meeting only shows people one of them. A new manager hears you're against everything. At parties you're the interesting one nobody invites to the next thing. Try agreeing with someone new about something, out loud, early. Disagree later, once they know you.

sun.upright:
A Pisces Sun and the King of Swords could hardly be more different. You're here to feel for people, imagine, help, and sometimes to disappear a bit into whatever needs you. He draws clear lines, weighs things coolly and says what he's decided. There's no clash between water and air, and no natural ease, so the two of you need introducing. It's worth doing, even if it's awkward at first.

Jupiter rules Pisces traditionally, Neptune in the modern scheme, and both of them make the edges soft. You see every point of view, you forgive easily, and you can find yourself agreeing to things you never meant to. Pisces has The Moon as its Major, all half-light and uncertain paths, and the King has no patience for half-light. His clarity can feel harsh to you, even unkind. Then you notice how much better people are helped when you've been clear with them, and how much less resentful you are afterwards.

At work this looks like the role where you speak up for people, and you'll do it better with the facts in order. In a relationship it's saying what you need, plainly, before it turns into a vague sadness. A friend who leans on you a lot may need to hear how much help you can actually give. Choose one thing you've been drifting on and make a clear decision about it, however small.
sun.reversed:
The King reversed on a Pisces Sun often shows up as a person, someone cold and certain who's been making decisions for you, a boss, a partner, a parent, and you've gone along because arguing feels impossible. Mutable water adapts to whatever it's poured into, and that includes a rigid container. Or it's your own mind turned harsh, judging yourself for being soft, pushing feeling away and going brittle in the process.

You may be accepting a manager's word without checking it, or letting a partner win every argument because you run out of words first. Neptune and Jupiter make it easy to let someone else be sure for you. Write down what you actually think about the decision they made. Read it back, and take it seriously.

moon.upright:
Every room has a mood, and a Pisces Moon soaks it up. You feel what others are feeling, often before they do, and you need time alone afterwards to wring it out. This King is a sharp card to land in that water. Water and air don't clash, but they don't mix easily either, and what the King brings is a very useful question for someone like you. Whose feeling is this.

That's the practical gift of this draw. Mutable water takes the shape of what's around it, and Jupiter and Neptune, the old and modern rulers of Pisces, both loosen the edges further. So you come home from a family visit feeling awful and can't work out why, and the answer is that the awfulness belonged to someone else. The King can sort that. He looks at it coolly and says that's your mother's worry, and it can stay hers. His coolness might feel like betraying the people you love. It isn't. It means you can keep being kind to them and still get a decent night's sleep.

With family, it means being able to visit and come home as yourself. With a partner it's knowing the difference between their bad day and yours. Sleep and dreams, which are often busy for you, tend to calm down when you've drawn a line during the day. After a hard conversation, ask yourself what part of the heaviness is yours, and leave the rest at the door.
moon.reversed:
With the King reversed on a Pisces Moon, you may have shut your feelings down because they got too much, and you're getting through on logic and not much else. It works for a while. Mutable water isn't made to stay frozen, though, and the feeling will leak out somewhere, usually in sleep or tiredness or tears at an advert. Or the King is a hard voice nearby, someone whose cold reasoning keeps making you doubt what you feel.

A partner's logic gets agreed to, and then you quietly grieve what you gave up. Your body carries an exhaustion that sleep doesn't fix. Give yourself somewhere safe to feel it, a bath, a long walk, music you love, and let it come without explaining it to anyone.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising tends to come across soft and a little hard to pin down. People see their own mood reflected back and like you for it. With the King of Swords as the card on your Ascendant, they're getting something firmer. There's a clear view under the gentleness, and strangers notice you know your own mind. Water and air have to be introduced, and when the introduction takes, you come across as kind and quietly sure.

Mutable water on the doorway usually adapts to the room. Jupiter and Neptune, the rulers of your Ascendant, make that adapting easy and a little dreamy. The King doesn't adapt. He holds his position and waits for the room to come to him, and you're trying that for once. It feels exposed, like standing in the open without your usual camouflage. You may catch yourself about to go along with someone, and then say what you think.

At work this is being taken seriously in meetings where you used to be overlooked. In a new friendship it's setting the plan yourself for once. With a partner it's saying where you'd like to eat, and meaning it. With a pushy stranger, a salesperson or a difficult official, it's staying polite and not budging. When someone new asks what you'd like, answer with the first true thing that comes to mind.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising with this card upside down can send very mixed signals. You're gentle and then suddenly sharp, dreamy and then oddly cold, and people don't know which version they've met. The reversed King puts a hard edge on a soft entrance, often because you're defending yourself from being taken advantage of again. Or the King belongs to someone else, a forceful person you've just met who's already deciding things for you, and you're letting them.

A new colleague is surprised by how blunt your email was after how sweet you were in person. A friend of a friend talks you into plans you didn't want. Before you agree to anything with someone new, give yourself a day. Say 'let me think about it' and mean it.

1.upright:
The first house is you as you walk through the door, your body, your manner, the way you start anything. It's angular, one of the chart's four corners, so whatever lands here gets seen. With the King of Swords in it, people see a clear head and a steady manner, and you're starting things on your own terms. Mercury has its joy in the first house, an old way of saying the mind is happy here, and for a card that's all mind, that matters.

Aries is the first house's natural sign and Mars its natural ruler, so this corner likes to act fast, and air and fire help each other along. The King's contribution is thinking before moving. You'll feel it as a new reluctance to leap, and a new confidence once you've decided. For anyone used to going on instinct there's some tension in that. Being more considered can feel like being less yourself. People can tell you've thought about it, though, and they follow more readily.

In the body it can show as better posture, a straighter back, a steadier voice, the physical side of being sure. With appearance it might be a sharper, simpler look, the haircut or the jacket that says you mean business. In a new role or a new project it's the clear opening statement. Decide what you want people to know about you in the first minute, and say it.
1.reversed:
In the first house the reversed King makes you come across harder than you mean to. Your face, your tone, the way you hold yourself, it all says verdict, and people step back before you've said much. The Mars side of this house wants action, and the reversed card gives it a cold edge, so you can seem impatient and critical in a way you'd be surprised to see on film. Mercury's joy here means your words get noticed, and they're sharper than your intentions.

The body holds it as tension in the jaw and shoulders, or a headache from keeping everything tight. New situations bring people who keep their distance. Loosen something physical, a stretch, a walk, your hands unclenched in meetings. Then smile at someone before you speak.

2.upright:
Money you can actually count, and the self-worth that goes with it, is second-house territory. What you earn, what you own, what you think you deserve. It's a succedent house, where things get built up and held on to. The King of Swords brings a clear head into it, and a clear head about money is rarer than it should be. Taurus is the natural sign here and Venus the ruler, earth and comfort, while the King is air, and the friction between those opposed elements is between what you think about money and what you actually do with it.

Most people have a gap there. You believe you should save, and the spending happens anyway. You know what you're worth, and you still quote low. The King has no patience for that gap. He wants the numbers looked at honestly and a fair decision made. That's uncomfortable, because the comfort habits are comfortable for a reason, and Venus doesn't like being told no. It's also, usually, a huge relief once it's done.

At work this is the pay conversation, done with the facts, what the role pays elsewhere and what you've delivered. At home it's the joint budget, sat down and sorted without anyone being blamed. With your own worth it's the fee you raise, or the unpaid favour you stop doing. Write down what you earn, what you spend and what you'd charge a stranger for your time, and look at all three together.
2.reversed:
Upside down in the second house, the King can turn money into a matter of control. Every purchase questioned, every bill a lecture, the budget run like a courtroom. Or you're so sure of your reasoning about money that you've stopped checking the actual numbers, and with air and earth opposed the theory runs away from the bank balance. It can also mean tying your worth entirely to what you earn and judging yourself coldly when it falls short.

Couples feel it as rows about spending where one person always has to justify themselves. At work it can be a low offer you've argued yourself into accepting. Look at the real figures before you decide anything about money, and get a second opinion from someone who isn't invested in the answer.

3.upright:
Everyday talk lives in the third house, messages, siblings, neighbours, short trips, the things you're learning. The house belongs naturally to Gemini and to Mercury, so this is air territory, and the King is air too. He's right at home, and that amplifies things, for better and for too much. Your voice is what's lit up. You're saying things clearly, putting them in writing, and being listened to.
