The third is a cadent house, where things get processed and adjusted, and it's where the Moon has its joy, which ties it to ordinary daily life. So the King's clarity shows up in small daily ways. Emails that get straight to the point. A text that settles a muddle. The too-much side is the sharp tongue. With the element doubled, a clever put-down comes very easily, and you might find you've said the precise, cutting thing before you meant to.

With a brother or sister it can be the honest conversation that's been building for years, done calmly for once. With neighbours it's settling the parking or the fence with a clear, fair note. In study it's the course that sharpens your thinking, or the exam where you write well under pressure. Before you send anything important, read it back as the person getting it, and take one sharp line out.
3.reversed:
The King reversed in the third house tends to show as words used as weapons. The sarcastic reply, the email that's technically polite and designed to wound, the argument with a sibling where you bring up something from twenty years ago because you can. The element's doubled here, and upside down it gets quick and cold. Or it goes the other way and you can't say anything clearly at all, and messages sit unanswered because you can't find the right tone.

Family group chats are where it flares, and short sharp exchanges with neighbours, and a tense commute. Learning can stall too, because you've decided you already know. Write the reply you want to send, then sleep on it. Send the version you'd be happy to hear read out.

4.upright:
Home is the fourth house, the actual house or flat and the family behind it, the roots, the private ground nobody else sees. It's angular, one of the chart's corners, so what happens here shapes everything else. By nature it's Cancer's house, ruled by the Moon, which makes it the most feeling part of the chart. The King of Swords walks into that with a clear head and a set of principles. Air and water don't fight, but they have to be introduced, and the introduction is the work.

Something at home needs a fair, reasoned decision. It might be practical, the lease, the mortgage, the move, who pays for what. It might be the family, a parent getting older, a sibling who isn't pulling their weight, an old rule nobody questions. The King often turns up here as a person, a father or whichever relative has always been the judge. Bringing reason into a place full of feeling can seem cold. Most families are quietly relieved when someone finally says what's fair.

With property this could be reading the contract properly, or deciding to sell. With parents it's the conversation about care, money or the will, done calmly, with the facts. In your own home it's setting a household rule, screens at dinner or who does the bins, and keeping it consistently. Choose the thing at home everyone's been avoiding. Raise it at a calm moment, with a suggestion ready.
4.reversed:
When the King is reversed in the fourth house, home can start to feel like a tribunal. Rules enforced coldly, feelings dismissed as unreasonable, someone at the head of the table who's always right. That someone might be you, or a parent whose voice still runs things long after you've moved out. The Moon rules this house by nature, and the reversed King shuts the Moon out. Air and water never got a proper introduction here, and it shows.

It shows in a household where people go quiet when a certain person walks in. It shows in the family conversation about money or care that turns into a ruling nobody agreed to. Say one warm thing at home that has nothing to do with who's right. If there's a rule in the house nobody believes in, drop it.

5.upright:
Romance, creative work, children, and whatever you do purely for fun, that's the fifth house. It's Leo's house by nature, ruled by the Sun, and Venus has her joy here, so it's warm, fond, pleasure-seeking ground. The King's a serious man to find at the party. His air does feed the fire here, though, and what he brings to play is clarity and a bit of discipline.

With creative work that's often exactly right. The idea you've been playing with for ages is ready for a clear structure, an edit, a deadline, someone's honest opinion. In romance it's being straight about what you want early, which can be a relief for both of you. The tension is that the King can take the fun out of things. A hobby turns into a project with targets. A date becomes an assessment. You'll notice if you're doing it, because the pleasure goes flat.

With children, yours or anyone's you look after, it's being fair and consistent, the same rule on a good day and a bad one. With a creative project it's finishing the draft and showing it to someone whose judgement you trust. In love it's saying what you're looking for without playing games. Pick one thing you do for fun and give it some structure, but keep one evening a week for doing it badly.
5.reversed:
Reversed in the fifth, the King can drain the joy out of things. You're critiquing your own creative work before it's had a chance, or holding a date at a distance and grading them. Venus has her joy in this house, and the reversed King is poor company for her. Or you've gone cold on romance altogether and decided it's not worth the bother, on very logical grounds.

With children it can be strictness that's tipped into coldness, or a rule kept for the sake of winning. With a hobby it's the thing you used to love that's become another thing you're bad at. The Sun rules this house, and it needs warmth to do anything. Do something creative with no aim at all, and no audience, and don't judge it afterwards.

6.upright:
Daily routine is sixth-house business, and it's the actual routine. Your workload, the tasks nobody sees, and the upkeep of your body, sleep, food, exercise, the appointments. Virgo is its natural sign and Mercury its ruler, so it already has a thinking side, and Mars has his joy here, which is why it's a house of effort. The King brings order and judgement, and the friction is that he's air and this house is earth, so the plan and the practice don't automatically meet.

You may be very clear about how things should run. The new system at work, the health plan, the morning routine. The King's gift is working out the fair and sensible version and sticking to it. The risk is that it stays a plan, a beautiful spreadsheet and the same tired body. Sometimes the King is a person here, a manager or a colleague who's clear, fair and exacting.

At work it might be streamlining the way your team does things, and being the one who writes it down. With your health it's getting proper information from someone qualified and then following the advice, not just reading about it. With a boss like the King, it's respecting the standard and asking plainly for what you need. Choose one daily habit and do it at the same time every day, whether you feel like it or not.
6.reversed:
A critical boss is the classic sixth-house form of this King reversed, or you being one. Standards so high nobody meets them, feedback that's correct and crushing, a routine run like a regime. With the body it can be over-control, the rigid diet, the exercise plan that punishes, reading every symptom online and deciding the worst. Mars has his joy here, and the reversed card turns that effort cold.

The people who work with you feel it first, and then your body does, in tension and poor sleep. Take the routine down a notch. Keep the parts that help and drop the one that's become a punishment, and if a health worry keeps circling, take it to someone qualified and let them decide.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite you. A partner, a spouse, a business partner, the other side of a contract, even an open rival. It's angular, a corner of the chart, so what happens here is visible and decisive. Libra and Venus are its natural sign and ruler, which makes it air territory, and with the King of Swords here the element doubles. Fairness is the whole subject.

The King often arrives in the seventh as a person. Someone clear, honest and principled, who says what they mean and expects the same back. It might be a partner, or a lawyer, a mediator, a business contact who's hard to fool. With the element amplified, relationships run on straight talk, which is a relief if there's been too much guessing. The too much is a partnership that's all reasoning. You agree on everything sensible and never quite feel close. Venus rules this house and Venus wants warmth as well as fairness.

In a relationship it can mean the calm, honest conversation about what each of you actually wants from the next few years. In business it's reading the contract, asking the awkward question and getting the terms fair. In a dispute, a divorce or a falling-out between partners, it's a fair settlement reached without cruelty. Say plainly what you want from the person across from you, and then ask them the same.
7.reversed:
With the King reversed in the seventh, a relationship can turn into a debate. Every disagreement becomes a case, one person always wins on logic, and the other stops raising things. It might be you who's winning, or it might be a partner who uses reason to control. In business it can be a contract that's technically fair and quietly one-sided, or a lawyer who's more interested in winning than resolving.

It shows in the argument you won and the distance afterwards, and in the negotiation where someone got the better of you on paper. If you're the one winning, lose one on purpose and see what the other person says when they're not defending themselves. If you're the one losing, get independent advice.

8.upright:
Joint money, debts, tax and inheritance belong to the eighth house, and so does intimacy, sex and trust and the deep kind of closeness that needs both. It's also the house of endings. Scorpio is its natural sign, with Mars as the old ruler and Pluto the modern, and it's a water house. The King is air, a stranger here, and the two have to be introduced. When they are, you get honesty in the one place most people avoid it.

What the King does in the eighth is name things. What's owed, whose money is whose, what's actually going on in the bedroom, what needs to end. That can feel cold in a house this intimate, and some people will flinch. It also clears the air in a way nothing else does. The tension is that fixed water wants to feel its way through and keep things private, and the King wants it said and settled.

With shared money it's the joint account, the loan to family or the will, sorted fairly and written down. In a relationship it's the honest conversation about intimacy and trust, which might be the most important talk you have with a partner in years. Around an ending, a separation or a job or a death in the family, it's dealing with the practical side clearly so the feeling has room. Pick the conversation about shared money or trust you've been dodging, and have it calmly.
8.reversed:
Reversed in the eighth, the King can turn intimacy into control. Money used as leverage, secrets kept as insurance, a partner who's cold in bed or in the accounts and calls it being rational. Or you're the one keeping a clinical distance from something that frightens you, a debt, a loss, a need, and treating it like a problem to be managed. Fixed water holds on hard, and the reversed King gives it rules to hold on with.

It shows in the joint finances nobody talks about, and in a closeness that's gone mechanical. After an ending it shows as the legal side dealt with perfectly and the grief not dealt with at all. Choose one person you trust and tell them what you're actually afraid of here. Get proper advice on the money.

9.upright:
The ninth house is about the big questions and the long view. What you believe, what you study, far-off places, law, teaching, publishing, anything that widens the world. In the natural chart it's Sagittarius's house, with Jupiter as ruler, and the Sun has its joy here, so it's a bright, open part of the chart. Air helps fire along, and the King brings a sharp, principled mind to it. Your thinking is being tested against bigger ideas.

The King in the ninth is the scholar, the judge, the teacher who knows the subject cold. You may find you want to learn something properly, to the level where you could defend it, and that's the right instinct. The tension is conviction. The ninth is where beliefs get formed, and the King forms them firmly. That's good when you've done the reading. It's less good when a view hardens before you've heard the best argument against it.

In study it's the course, the qualification or the serious book that sharpens your view. With travel it's a trip to learn something, or planning a big move with the facts in hand. In legal matters it's getting good advice and following it. With a teacher or mentor it's the honest feedback you asked for. Pick one thing you believe and read the best case against it, written by someone smart.
9.reversed:
The King reversed in the ninth can harden belief into dogma. You've decided what's true, about politics or faith or how life works, and you've stopped listening. Or someone else's certainty is running your thinking, a teacher, a religion, an expert whose word you take without checking. Jupiter rules this house and enlarges whatever's in it, including rigid opinions. Air feeds the fire of this house, and with the card reversed what it feeds is certainty.

It shows in the argument at a family gathering that nobody could win, in a course you've stopped enjoying because the lecturer won't allow questions, in a legal matter where someone's being inflexible. Travel can go the same way, the trip where you spent the whole time comparing everything to home. Find someone who disagrees with you and ask them to explain, with no intention of replying. Just listen.

10.upright:
Career lives at the top of the chart. The tenth house is your public role, your reputation, the work people know you for, and the people above you. It's angular, as visible as a house gets. Saturn rules it by nature and Capricorn is its sign, so it's earth, and it rewards results you can point to. The King is air, which puts him at odds with this house's element. He deals in judgement and principle, and the tenth mostly wants to know what got delivered.

That friction is the story. You may be moving into a role where your job is to decide, to set standards, to be the one whose call is final, and that's the King's territory. Saturn wants to see it produce something measurable. Good judgement that nobody can see the results of doesn't get much credit here. So the task is making your principles show up in outcomes, and being willing to be unpopular for a decision that's right. Sometimes the King is your boss, an exacting, fair-minded senior person whose opinion carries weight.

At work this might be a promotion into management, a board seat, a role as the person who signs things off. With your reputation it's being known as straight, which is worth more than being known as nice. With a senior figure it's asking for their honest assessment of your work and taking it on the chin. Write down the standard you want to be known for, and apply it the same way to everyone, yourself included.
10.reversed:
Upside down at the top of the chart, the King can mean authority gone cold. A boss who rules by fear and precedent, or you becoming one, enforcing the rules because they're the rules. Saturn rules this house and the reversed card makes it rigid. Or it's a reputation for being harsh that's started to go ahead of you, so people are wary before they've met you. Air and earth pull apart here, and the principle stops touching the real job.

It shows in a team that tells you what you want to hear, in a decision made on principle that ignored the people it landed on, in a promotion that went to someone warmer. Ask someone you trust at work how you're seen. Take the answer without arguing, and change one thing.

11.upright:
Friends, groups, networks, causes and your hopes for the future are eleventh-house matters. Aquarius is its natural sign, Saturn its old ruler and Uranus the modern one, and Jupiter has his joy here, so it's a lucky, sociable, forward-looking house. It's air territory, and the King of Swords makes it doubly so. Your judgement is being noticed in a group.

You may find yourself running something, a committee, a club, a campaign, a group chat that needs a grown-up. People trust you to be fair and to say the awkward thing when it needs saying. The amplified air helps you see what the group actually wants and what's realistic. The too-much is detachment. You can be so principled about the group that you stop being a friend to anyone in it, and friends can feel that.

With friends it's being the honest one, the person they ask when they need the truth about the relationship or the business idea. With a cause or a community group it's being the one who reads the constitution and chairs the difficult meeting well. With your hopes it's getting clear about what you actually want in the next few years and saying it. Tell one friend something you admire about them, and one thing you'd change about the group, in the same conversation.
11.reversed:
The eleventh house with the King reversed can mean a friendship group that's turned into a court. Someone's been judged, sides have been taken, and the chat is full of carefully worded messages. It might be you who's sitting in judgement. Doubled air can do this, turn a group of friends into a set of positions. Or you've gone so detached that you've drifted away from people who counted on you, telling yourself it's nothing personal.

It shows in the committee meeting that became a power struggle, in the friend you've quietly dropped, in hopes you've argued yourself out of. Jupiter has his joy in this house, and the reversed King leaves very little room for his generosity. Reach out to one friend you've gone cold on, and don't make them explain anything. Just ask how they are.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is the part of life nobody sees. Retreat, sleep, dreams, the habits you don't talk about, what you're carrying that you haven't named. Its natural sign is Pisces, with Jupiter as the old ruler and Neptune the modern, and it's water, so the King's air has to be introduced to it. Saturn has his joy here, oddly, which is an old way of saying that discipline does well in private. That suits this King.

What he brings to the twelfth is a clear look at things you usually keep in the fog. The pattern that keeps tripping you up. The judgement of yourself you've never said aloud, harsher than anything you'd say to a friend. Some of that clarity will come in quiet time, on a long walk, in a notebook, in the middle of the night. It can be uncomfortable for a day or two, and then something usually loosens.

With therapy or counselling it's a clear, useful session, the one where something clicks. With sleep it's noticing what the mind's chewing on at three in the morning and writing it down. With the late-night scrolling or the extra drink, it's seeing the habit clearly without beating yourself up. With solitude it's time alone that's for thinking, not hiding. Book an hour alone somewhere quiet, and write down the one thing you've been avoiding looking at.
12.reversed:
In the twelfth, a reversed King tends to mean a harsh voice running out of sight. You're judging yourself constantly, in private, and nobody knows. Or you're using logic to keep something buried, a grief, a fear, an old hurt, reasoning it away every time it surfaces. Neptune and Jupiter rule this house and want things to dissolve, and the reversed King won't let them. Saturn's joy here can turn into a very private kind of strictness.

It shows in bad sleep, in a low mood you can't explain, in a habit you use to switch off. People close to you may only see that you've gone quiet. Tell a counsellor, or one trusted person, what the voice in your head actually says. Then ask them what they'd say back.
